message.content:
Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) belong to very different lineages within mammals—lion is a member of the order **Carnivora** (family Felidae), while zebra is a member of the order **Perissodactyla** (family Equidae). Their most recent common ancestor is therefore at the level of the clade of placental mammals that includes both of these orders.

In phylogenetic terms, the common ancestor of lion and zebra is the ancestor of the super‑order **Laurasiatheria**, which encompasses several orders of mammals including Carnivora, Perissodactyla, Cetartiodactyla, Chiroptera, and others. This ancestor lived tens of millions of years ago, long before the diversification of the modern families of cats and horses.
